scenarios.hypothesis: A signature-valid synthetic component is accepted even when its signer is not authorized by the active secure-boot policy generation for the selected stage.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled emulator and mock verifier report only an inert component marker plus the policy decision; no arbitrary payload is executed or persisted.
scenarios.positive_control: The same synthetic component signed by the current authorized lab signer is selected, verified, loaded into an inert sink, and correlated to the current boot receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: Keep component bytes and boot path constant while switching to a synthetic signer that remains cryptographically valid but is absent from the active policy generation.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the test would require production signing material, irreversible fuse changes, persistent security disablement, destructive flashing, or any non-owned device.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation the stale-policy signer is rejected at the signer-authorization transition while the current synthetic signer still reaches the inert next-stage marker.
scenarios.root_of_trust_identity: Synthetic root ROT-LAB-20-A is pinned in the emulator fixture and its identifier is captured from the verifier policy lookup rather than inferred from storage contents.
scenarios.verification_policy_generation: Policy generation POLICY-G7 is the authoritative current generation; POLICY-G6 remains available only as a deliberately stale counterfactual fixture.
scenarios.boot_mode_path: Release-like emulator path MODE-R uses the normal first-stage-to-second-stage transition with debug and manufacturing modes disabled in the fixture.
scenarios.selector_state: Selector state chooses synthetic slot A and component class stage2 from authenticated fixture metadata with retry and fallback counters pinned to baseline values.
scenarios.candidate_component_identity: Candidate component STAGE2-A-G7 is identified by a synthetic manifest identity and marker digest before signature or policy authorization is evaluated.
scenarios.candidate_digest_version: The fixture records deterministic digest DIGEST-STAGE2-A and semantic version 20.7 so bytes and freshness can be compared independently of signer identity.
scenarios.signer_identity: Signer LAB-SIGNER-CURRENT and counterfactual LAB-SIGNER-STALE use synthetic keys created only for this fixture and never correspond to production credentials.
scenarios.signer_authorization_decision: The oracle records whether the active POLICY-G7 authorizes the presented signer for stage2, independently from whether the cryptographic signature verifies.
scenarios.rollback_domain_generation: Rollback domain STAGE2 has authoritative generation RB-42 and both controls use the same current generation so signer authority is the only changed dimension.
scenarios.selected_component_identity: The selector receipt must identify STAGE2-A-G7 as the selected component before the loader is allowed to consume any component bytes.
scenarios.loaded_component_identity: The mock loader emits a read-only digest receipt for the exact inert component bytes delivered to the synthetic next stage, allowing selection and load identities to be compared.
scenarios.verified_loaded_binding: A correlation token binds verifier acceptance, selected component identity, mock-loader digest, and current boot generation without relying on a generic boot-success message.
scenarios.handoff_state_identity: Synthetic handoff object HANDOFF-G7 carries only non-sensitive marker data and the active policy-generation identifier expected by the inert next-stage consumer.
scenarios.next_stage_consumer: An inert mock stage2 consumer records the received component and handoff identifiers but performs no privileged operation and executes no untrusted functionality.
scenarios.alternate_recovery_path: Recovery is disabled for the primary assertion and separately exercised as a negative-equivalence control so normal-path signer authority cannot be generalized by assumption.
scenarios.bounded_boot_result: The only bounded result is an emulator transition to the inert stage2 marker with a deterministic receipt; no host modification or persistent device state is created.
scenarios.receipt_attestation_binding: Receipt REC-G7 binds boot generation, policy generation, selected component, loaded digest, and inert result so a prior or unrelated boot cannot satisfy the oracle.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: The fixture increments policy/boot generation between stale and current controls and clears selector/verifier caches before each run to prevent inherited authority.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Repeat the same component and boot path with only signer authorization changed between current POLICY-G7 and stale/unauthorized signer identity, expecting opposite decisions.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: The review excludes development mode, stale verifier cache, previous-generation receipts, recovery fallback, and a different file being loaded than the verified candidate.
scenarios.evidence_level: BC5 — causal proof only after the bounded synthetic acceptance and every authority, load, generation, counterfactual, and remediation binding is satisfied.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: BC5 — the case is capped below BC5 whenever signer authorization, selected-to-loaded identity, generation correlation, or remediation regression remains unproven.

scenarios.hypothesis: A stale synthetic component can be selected or loaded after the authoritative rollback generation advances because selection/load identity is not bound to the freshness decision.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled emulator uses synthetic A/B slots and a mock loader that returns only read-only component markers and digest receipts without executing component code.
scenarios.positive_control: Current slot B component at rollback generation RB-43 passes freshness policy, is selected, and reaches the inert next-stage sink with matching verifier and loader receipts.
scenarios.negative_control: Hold signer and component class constant while presenting a stale RB-42 component or stale slot-selection state after the authoritative domain has advanced to RB-43.
scenarios.stop_condition: Abort and stop if validation would write irreversible rollback fuses, destructively flash owned hardware, alter production counters, or touch an unauthorized target.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: The stale generation or stale-slot path is rejected before loading, while the current RB-43 slot B component still verifies, loads, and produces the expected inert receipt.
scenarios.root_of_trust_identity: Synthetic root ROT-LAB-20-B remains constant across controls so the experiment isolates rollback and selected-versus-loaded binding rather than root changes.
scenarios.verification_policy_generation: Verification policy POLICY-G8 authorizes the same synthetic signer in both controls and is pinned as current for the entire deterministic scenario.
scenarios.boot_mode_path: Release-like A/B emulator boot path uses normal fallback logic with retry counters fixed except when a specific counterfactual explicitly changes selector generation.
scenarios.selector_state: Authenticated selector metadata marks slot B active for generation SLOT-G43 while a stale SLOT-G42 record is retained only as the negative-control input.
scenarios.candidate_component_identity: Candidate identifiers STAGE2-B-RB43 and STAGE2-A-RB42 are inert marker artifacts whose identities remain distinguishable at verification and loading boundaries.
scenarios.candidate_digest_version: Deterministic digests and versions encode RB43-current versus RB42-stale identity so freshness can be traced without executing either component.
scenarios.signer_identity: Both candidate components use the same synthetic LAB-SIGNER-ROLLBACK identity, preventing signer authorization from explaining the expected freshness difference.
scenarios.signer_authorization_decision: POLICY-G8 authorizes LAB-SIGNER-ROLLBACK for this component class in both controls, and that decision is captured independently of rollback evaluation.
scenarios.rollback_domain_generation: Authoritative rollback domain STAGE2 is RB-43; the fixture records candidate generation, stored generation, comparison result, and commit epoch before selection/load.
scenarios.selected_component_identity: The selector must report the component identity chosen after freshness evaluation, including slot and selector generation, rather than only reporting a slot label.
scenarios.loaded_component_identity: Mock loader reports the digest and synthetic marker actually delivered from the selected slot so stale cache or wrong-slot reads cannot masquerade as current selection.
scenarios.verified_loaded_binding: Verifier receipt, rollback decision, selector receipt, and mock-loader digest share the current boot correlation identity and must agree on component generation.
scenarios.handoff_state_identity: Handoff object HANDOFF-RB43 records the accepted rollback and slot generation for inspection by an inert next-stage consumer without granting any extra authority.
scenarios.next_stage_consumer: The inert consumer checks only marker identity and handoff generation and records a read-only result, avoiding arbitrary execution or persistent state changes.
scenarios.alternate_recovery_path: A separate recovery-path control confirms stale rollback state is not accepted merely because fallback/recovery selection follows a neighboring code path.
scenarios.bounded_boot_result: Bounded success is limited to the mock loader and inert consumer acknowledging the current marker; stale input must stop before that controlled transition.
scenarios.receipt_attestation_binding: Synthetic receipt REC-RB43 binds rollback comparison, selector generation, loaded digest, and boot generation so delayed logs cannot satisfy the oracle.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: The scenario advances from RB-42/SLOT-G42 to RB-43/SLOT-G43 and resets emulator caches between runs to make stale-generation acceptance observable.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Repeat with identical signer and policy but switch only current-versus-stale rollback/slot generation, then separately distinguish verified candidate from mock-loaded bytes.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: The review rules out expected failed-boot fallback, retry-counter changes, stale selector cache, delayed receipts, development exceptions, and loading from a different slot than reported.
scenarios.evidence_level: BC5 — causal proof requires bounded stale-generation acceptance tied through rollback decision, selector identity, actual loaded bytes, counterfactual, and regression.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: BC5 — cap below causal proof if rollback state is observed only in metadata, selected-versus-loaded identity is ambiguous, or fallback semantics remain unexplained.

scenarios.hypothesis: A recovery or alternate boot path accepts stale or unauthenticated handoff security state even though the normal path verifies the component under the current policy generation.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled emulator routes synthetic normal and recovery paths into an inert next-stage consumer that records read-only handoff identities and no executable payload.
scenarios.positive_control: The current recovery fixture uses the authorized policy generation and authenticated HANDOFF-G9 object, reaching the inert consumer with all component and receipt identities aligned.
scenarios.negative_control: Keep verified component bytes constant while substituting a stale HANDOFF-G8 generation or an alternate-path policy context that should no longer authorize that handoff state.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop before any test requires real recovery signing keys, permanent boot-policy changes, destructive flashing, security-feature disablement, or interaction with a third-party device.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After the fix the stale/unauthenticated recovery handoff is rejected while both the current normal path and authorized current recovery path retain their intended inert behavior.
scenarios.root_of_trust_identity: Synthetic root ROT-LAB-20-C is shared by normal and recovery fixtures so path equivalence can be evaluated against the same owned root identity.
scenarios.verification_policy_generation: Current policy POLICY-G9 explicitly defines normal and recovery signer/handoff rules, while stale POLICY-G8 is retained only for a generation counterfactual.
scenarios.boot_mode_path: The scenario records NORMAL-G9 and RECOVERY-G9 path identities independently, including the selector reason and transition that entered recovery mode.
scenarios.selector_state: Synthetic selector state fixes component choice while varying only path/handoff generation, preventing ordinary slot fallback from explaining a recovery-specific result.
scenarios.candidate_component_identity: The same inert component STAGE2-C-G9 is the candidate on both paths, allowing the experiment to isolate path policy and handoff-state authority.
scenarios.candidate_digest_version: A deterministic digest and version for STAGE2-C-G9 are recorded before path divergence so component-byte differences cannot explain the observed handoff decision.
scenarios.signer_identity: Synthetic signer LAB-SIGNER-RECOVERY-G9 is authorized according to explicit POLICY-G9 path rules and never represents production or vendor signing material.
scenarios.signer_authorization_decision: The trace records path-specific signer authorization separately from handoff-state validation so a valid recovery signature cannot silently authorize stale handoff data.
scenarios.rollback_domain_generation: Rollback domain remains current at RB-44 across both paths, isolating handoff and alternate-path generation rather than component freshness as the tested dimension.
scenarios.selected_component_identity: Both normal and recovery selector receipts identify the same current inert component, with path identity preserved as a separate authoritative field.
scenarios.loaded_component_identity: Mock loader digest confirms both paths deliver the same inert component bytes, preventing a hidden recovery-image difference from explaining the result.
scenarios.verified_loaded_binding: Verification, selection, and mock-loader receipts are correlated to the current boot generation before handoff validation is evaluated by the inert consumer.
scenarios.handoff_state_identity: HANDOFF-G9 is the authenticated current object; HANDOFF-G8 is a synthetic stale object with distinguishable generation and otherwise equivalent benign contents.
scenarios.next_stage_consumer: The inert next-stage consumer validates handoff generation/path binding and records accept/reject plus marker identity without performing privileged or destructive behavior.
scenarios.alternate_recovery_path: Recovery is the primary alternate-path subject and is compared directly with the normal path; neither path is assumed equivalent without root/policy/handoff evidence.
scenarios.bounded_boot_result: The bounded result is only an inert consumer acknowledgement for current HANDOFF-G9; stale HANDOFF-G8 must not cross the controlled handoff transition.
scenarios.receipt_attestation_binding: Receipt REC-HANDOFF-G9 binds path identity, boot generation, loaded digest, handoff generation, consumer decision, and bounded result to prevent stale correlation.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: The fixture advances policy and handoff state from generation G8 to G9, resets recovery/selector caches, and records the transition epoch for every run.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Use identical current component bytes while toggling only HANDOFF-G9 versus stale HANDOFF-G8, then compare normal and recovery paths under the same synthetic root/policy generation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: The review excludes documented recovery exceptions, stale telemetry, previous-boot receipts, debug/manufacturing mode, unexpected fallback, cache retention, and component-byte differences.
scenarios.evidence_level: BC5 — causal proof requires bounded stale-handoff acceptance on the alternate path plus current generation bindings, counterfactual controls, and remediation regression.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: BC5 — cap evidence below BC5 if recovery policy equivalence, handoff authentication/generation, selected-to-loaded identity, or receipt correlation is not independently proven.
